edges.description: The sleeplessness of FFI is a failure to generate sleep, not a failure to maintain it: the thalamic lesion removes the oscillator that builds NREM sleep.

Multisystem degeneration is a plausible substrate for the motor syndrome that includes myoclonus. The cited clinicopathologic series does not identify the generator of the jerks or exclude a thalamic contribution.

edges.description: Cortical gliosis and spongiform change involve the motor cortex and its descending projections, producing the pyramidal signs.
Swallowing failure appears with the advanced multisystem degeneration and is grouped with the other motor abnormalities in the clinical literature.
intermediate_mechanisms: The sources group dysphagia with the FFI motor abnormalities but do not localize it to a specific bulbar lesion, so the intervening step is not established.

edges.description: Generalized seizures occur in codon-129 heterozygotes, the group with the more extensive cortical involvement.
Earlier sphincter loss likewise tracks with the more extensive cortical involvement of the codon-129 heterozygous group.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of cortical continence control is inferred from the co-occurrence with extensive cortical involvement; no lesion-level localization is reported.

nodes.description: The D178N substitution, in cis with 129M, renders PrP-C prone to adopting the misfolded, self-templating conformer that seeds propagation. Recombinant human PrP carrying the FFI M129/D178N haplotype is markedly aggregation-prone: unlike the GSS (P102L) and familial CJD (E200K) variants, which are recovered soluble, the D178N protein partitions into inclusion bodies. This is a gain of toxic conformation, not a loss of PrP function.

nodes.description: Destruction of thalamic relay and reticular circuitry abolishes the thalamocortical oscillations that generate sleep spindles, K-complexes, and slow-wave sleep. The result is not ordinary insomnia but a failure to build sleep: spindles and K-complexes disappear early, NREM sleep is eventually abolished, and only brief residual REM periods without atonia persist, intruding into wakefulness as enacted dreams. FFI is the clinical experiment that implicated the thalamus as necessary for sleep generation.

nodes.description: FFI is thalamus-dominant but not thalamus-only. Beyond the defining thalamic lesion, the same disease process damages the inferior olives, the cerebellum (atrophy with axonal torpedoes), and the cerebral cortex (gliosis, and spongiform change in some cases). These lesions are primary rather than secondary to the thalamic damage, and they provide a plausible substrate for the somatomotor syndrome - ataxia, dysarthria, myoclonus, pyramidal signs - although individual symptom generators are not all localized. Cortical features distinguish codon-129 heterozygotes, who show more extensive cortical involvement on PET and at autopsy. Because neocortical PrPres accumulation rises with disease duration, this component is more prominent in the prolonged 129MV course.

nodes.description: The defining lesion: marked neuronal depletion and astrocytic gliosis concentrated in the mediodorsal and anteroventral thalamic nuclei, with inferior olivary hypertrophy and only limited cortical spongiosis. The mediodorsal nucleus appears intrinsically more vulnerable - it sustains severe neuronal loss at relatively moderate PrP-Sc burden - which is why FFI is a thalamic disease rather than a diffuse encephalopathy.

nodes.description: The autocatalytic core of the disease: a misfolded PrP molecule recruits and refolds native PrP-C, so that the conformation itself acts as the replicating template. In FFI the resulting protease-resistant core is a 19 kDa (type 2) fragment with marked underrepresentation of the unglycosylated glycoform - a molecular signature distinct from the 21 kDa fragment of sporadic and other inherited prion diseases. Inoculation of FFI brain extract into chimeric human-mouse PrP transgenic mice reproduces the 19 kDa fragment, establishing that conformation, not sequence, carries the strain information.
